title.narrative: Strengthened institutions, mechanisms and processes of social dialogue for promoting decent work

description.narrative: Lao PDR recognises the importance of social dialogue but the formal social dialogue mechanisms operate with varying degrees of effectiveness. The mechanisms face a number of challenges that need addressing, especially in the areas of representation, gender, functioning, follow up arrangements and support for implementation at provincial levels. In line with DWCP 2022-26, interventions aim at supporting constituents to improve practices of dialogue, strengthen labour relations cooperation, promote evidence-based wage policies and collective bargaining as industrial relations institution. 2024-25, sectoral social dialogue was strengthened in the tea and coffee sector through provincial stakeholder working groups that enabled tripartite representatives to address sector-specific challenges, improving access to social security and occupational safety and health. At the policy level, ILO support to the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and the Minimum Wage Task Force has strengthened the foundations for evidence-based wage setting. The approach integrates both economic factors and the needs of workers and their families, ensuring that minimum wage adjustments are balanced using socio-economic indicators and aligned with ILO Convention No. 131. The ILO methodology for estimating workers’ and their families’ needs was shared with national counterparts and, when available data from the Lao Expenditure and Consumption Survey, this allows to estimate household living costs to assess wage adequacy. The Government adopted a minimum wage adjustment and cost-of-living allowance raising total monthly pay for non-professional workers to at least LAK 2,500,000, and in addition a 2024 notification required foreign-currency wages to follow official exchange rates, protecting workers from wage erosion. The programme strengthens tripartism, industrial relations, and dialogue-driven policy making, promoting adequate wage setting to support decent work and social justice in Lao PDR.
